record.paper_title: Operations Research challenges in forestry: 33 open problems
record.original_question: Existing forest-routing approaches often treat truck routes independently and therefore ignore congestion and waiting at mills or self-loaders, even though synchronization constraints are needed to represent those interactions. The open question is how to design models and methods for the forestry VRP that correctly synchronize trucks with loaders and related shared resources.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9 How can we develop models and methods for the forestry VRP that deal with synchronization of trucks and loaders?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the forestry vehicle routing problem (forestry VRP) defined as follows. A fleet of heterogeneous log trucks must transport timber from a set of forest harvest sites (stands) to a set of demand points (mills or terminals) over a planning horizon. At each harvest site and at each mill there is a limited set of shared service resources—self-loaders (cranes) for loading at stands and unloading equipment at mills—whose availability is constrained in time and which can serve only one truck at a time. Each truck has a capacity and may or may not carry its own loader; trucks without onboard loaders must rely on a stationary or mobile loader being present and idle at the moment of (un)loading. A feasible plan assigns to each truck a sequence of trips (each trip consisting of an origin stand, a destination mill, a load type, and timing) such that:

(i) supply at stands and demand at mills are met within prescribed time windows;
(ii) for every loading or unloading event, the truck and the required loader (or unloading resource) are simultaneously present at the same location, i.e. their schedules are synchronized;
(iii) no two activities requiring the same resource overlap in time; and
(iv) standard routing constraints (capacity, working hours, compatibility of trucks with load types) hold.

The objective is to minimize total operating cost (e.g., a weighted sum of travel time, waiting time at stands and mills, and number of trucks used).

Develop mathematical optimization models and exact or heuristic solution methods for this synchronized forestry VRP that explicitly enforce the synchronization of trucks with loaders and other shared (un)loading resources, and that scale to instance sizes encountered in industrial practice.
artifact.status_search_result: Several recent works address synchronization of trucks and loaders in forestry VRPs, including constraint-programming and hybrid CP/MIP approaches to log-truck scheduling, a decomposition method for coordinated truck loading and routing, and exact approaches to full-truckload pickup-and-delivery with resource synchronization. These contribute partial solutions for specific variants and instance sizes, but a fully general, scalable modeling and solution framework for the synchronized forestry VRP remains an active area of research.

status_evidence.title: Coordinated Truck Loading and Routing Problem: A Forestry Logistics Case Study
status_evidence.snippet: Decomposition approach for optimization of log logistics considering synchronization of log loaders and heterogeneous trucks at cut blocks and sort yards.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work proposes a decomposition approach addressing loader–truck synchronization in forestry logistics.

status_evidence.title: A Hybrid Constraint Programming Approach to the Log-Truck Scheduling Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Synchronization of trucks (without crane) and loaders is required since loaders serve several stands.
status_evidence.claim: Hybrid CP/MIP methods have been proposed that explicitly model truck–loader synchronization.

status_evidence.title: Resources synchronization in a full truckload pickup and delivery problem: An exact approach
status_evidence.snippet: Exact approach for resource synchronization in full-truckload pickup and delivery.
status_evidence.claim: Exact methods exist for related full-truckload routing problems with resource synchronization.

status_evidence.title: A mathematical modeling for simultaneous routing and scheduling of logging trucks
status_evidence.snippet: Simultaneous routing and scheduling model for logging trucks in the forest supply chain.
status_evidence.claim: Combined routing-and-scheduling models for logging trucks have been developed, partially addressing the problem.
